description: Wildfires are becoming increasingly frequent due to global warming—which involves rising CO2 production—and the depletion of the ozone layer. A web application can harmonize these records into a calendar of fire activity based on active fire hotspots, enabling scientists and land managers to examine historical fire patterns, unusual conditions, and critical periods.
summary: This is a web application that displays hotspots where fires have been detected—though some of these may occasionally be false positives. It is a valuable tool, as it allows for analysis such as determining that if a region has gone a month without rain, the following month should be considered a high-risk period for forest fires. Furthermore, historical data from recent years can be crucial for identifying anomalies.
details: For this project, I used data from the api.meteomatics.com platform, NASA FIRMS, and reports from other official websites. The work was developed in Visual Studio with the aid of AI, and the project is hosted on GitHub.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS — Datos de focos activos VIIRS (NOAA-20, NOAA-21 y Suomi-NPP).
